theorems.hypotheses: stable finite non-negative rational transition-mass matrix W
theorems.statement: Z_loop(W)=det(I-W)^(-1)=det(W^star); if W=A/D and B=DI-A then Z_loop=D^n/det(B). Gamma(W)=LN(Z_loop)=-LN(det(I-W)) is a derived exact logarithmic readout.
theorems.prior_art_boundary: log-determinant, Neumann-series and graph-zeta determinant identities are classical

theorems.hypotheses: same stable finite rational scope; B=DI-A, delta=det(B), C=adj(B)
theorems.statement: h0=C*1 is a strictly positive integer vector and B h0=delta*1, equivalently A h0=D h0-delta*1. The canonical rational potential is x=(D/delta)h0.
theorems.boundary: h0 need not be primitive; primitive integer normalization changes the common slack

theorems.hypotheses: stable finite non-negative rational positive recurrence
theorems.statement: Gamma is invariant under positive diagonal vertex gauge, additive across SCC diagonal blocks, blind to feed-forward inter-SCC edges, and Gamma=0 iff the positive-support digraph is acyclic.
theorems.trace_form: Gamma=sum_{k>=1} tr(W^k)/k; standard primitive-loop Euler product is classical prior art

theorems.hypotheses: stable finite explicit positive branch system; edge e:a->b has weight q_e; S=(I-W)^(-1)
theorems.statement: R_e=dGamma/d ln(q_e)=q_e S_ba. R_e is exact rational, individually gauge invariant, and R_e>0 iff e lies on a directed cycle. Sum_e R_e=tr(S-I).

theorems.hypotheses: same explicit stable positive branch system; e:a->b and f:c->d
theorems.statement: H_ef=delta_ef q_e S_ba + q_e q_f S_bc S_da is symmetric exact rational and positive semidefinite. On a strongly connected recurrent support, ker(H) is exactly the vertex-gauge coboundary space and rank(H)=|E|-|V|+1, so H is positive definite on the cycle/gauge quotient.
theorems.general_graph: transient edges have zero Hessian rows/columns and cyclic SCCs form independent blocks

theorems.hypotheses: common explicit edge denominator D; q_e=a_e/D; B=DI-A; delta=det(B); C=adj(B)
theorems.statement: R_e=a_e C_ba/delta and H_ef=[delta_ef a_e C_ba delta + a_e a_f C_bc C_da]/delta^2. Thus first/second recurrent response has a symmetric integer numerator certificate.

theorems.hypotheses: finite non-negative rational W=A/D under uniform scaling tW
theorems.statement: p(t)=det(DI-tA) is an integer polynomial. If support is acyclic, p(t)=D^n and all t>=0 are stable. If a directed positive cycle exists, the finite stability endpoint t_c is the smallest positive real root of p(t).
theorems.boundary: t_c may be irrational; no floating spectral primitive or rational optimizer is assumed

theorems.statement: chi(t)=dGamma(t)/d ln(t)=-t p'(t)/p(t)=tr((I-tW)^(-1)-I) is exact rational. If the critical root has multiplicity r, chi(t)~r t_c/(t_c-t). Any rational stability potential h yields t_c>=1/alpha(h), alpha=max_i (Wh)_i/h_i.

theorems.hypotheses: finite graph with positive rational explicit edge weights and positive rational vertex gauge
theorems.statement: Q_{>0}^x is isomorphic to direct_sum_p Z by prime valuations and H^1(G;Q_{>0}^x) is isomorphic to direct_sum_p H^1(G;Z). Rational gauge acts primewise by integer coboundaries.
theorems.boundary: the faithful log-prime image is not generally a discrete Euclidean lattice

theorems.hypotheses: connected underlying finite graph, fixed root and spanning tree T
theorems.statement: There is a unique rational vertex gauge with root scale 1 and every tree-edge weight 1. The beta_1 non-tree weights are complete gauge coordinates and equal the fundamental algebraic cycle products; their prime valuations form a complete exact integer normal form.

theorems.hypotheses: positive rational gauge class and integer m>=2
theorems.statement: Prime valuation reduction mod m gives H^1(G;Q_{>0}^x)/m isomorphic to direct_sum_p H^1(G;Z/m). For m=2 each prime gives a typed C2/F2 holonomy shadow, and every finite-coefficient graph class has a positive rational p-power lift.

theorems.hypotheses: positive rational q and integer m>=2
theorems.statement: Writing v_p(q)=m k_p+r_p with 0<=r_p<m gives a unique q=s_m(q)t_m(q)^m where s_m is a positive m-power-free integer and t_m positive rational. After reducing q/s_m=N/M, N and M are exact m-th powers and t_m may be materialized through the existing BRC ROOT_m facade.
theorems.m2: q=s(q)r(q)^2 with squarefree s; s is the all-prime C2 parity skeleton and r the exact rational square-thickness root

theorems.hypotheses: finite directed multigraph with one explicit formal variable x_e per branch edge
theorems.statement: P_G(x)=det(I-W(x)) equals the signed sum over pairwise vertex-disjoint explicit directed cycle systems. P_G is multiaffine, every nonzero explicit-edge coefficient is +/-1, P_G is identically 1 iff the support is a DAG, and every cycle-system monomial is individually vertex-gauge invariant.
theorems.boundary: alternating determinant coefficients are inclusion-exclusion signs, not signed/amplitude BRC branch weights

theorems.hypotheses: stable positive specialization q of WBRC-T29 with P=P_G(q)>0
theorems.statement: R_e=-q_e P_e/P. P_e<=0, strictly iff e is recurrent. Multiaffinity gives H_ee=R_e(1+R_e); for e!=f, H_ef=q_e q_f(P_eP_f-P P_ef)/P^2>=0.

theorems.hypotheses: finite stable positive rational recurrent branch system
theorems.statement: The same recurrent object has a finite exclusion certificate P_G as an alternating sum over vertex-disjoint cycle systems and an infinite positive closure Z_loop=1/P_G, Gamma=-LN(P_G) as the closed-walk/primitive-loop expansion. Overlapping cycles excluded from one determinant term reappear through inversion/log closure.

negative_boundaries.statement: C2/mod-m holonomy shadows do not determine the full positive rational state, recurrent phase or loop surplus. Example: 1/2 and 2 share squarefree skeleton 2 but have stable/divergent phases; 1/2 and 1/8 share skeleton 2 but different stable loop-zeta ratios.
Full H^1(G;Q_{>0}^x) gauge data can be strictly richer than recurrent Gamma/R/H. Feed-forward diamond cross-ratios may be nontrivial while all directed recurrent loop observables vanish.
Signs (-1)^{number of disjoint cycles} in det(I-W) are finite inclusion-exclusion/permutation coefficients, not signed/amplitude branch weights in positive Weighted-BRC.
The prime-valuation gauge object is an abstract finite-support free-abelian module. Its faithful embedding sum v_p ln p into R is not generally a discrete Euclidean lattice.
Rational potentials give exact rational lower bounds on the critical scale, but no canonical rational Collatz/Perron optimizer is claimed; the exact critical scale may be irrational algebraic.
